findings.issue: Unnamed registry values cannot be represented and retrieved using their actual empty name. The core COM entries use the display label '(Default)', but model_context(path, value_name='') returns no value knowledge; '(Default)' returns the record. _research rejects empty name fields, preventing a faithful correction in data. A literal named value '(Default)' is also potentially conflated with the unnamed value by the current convention.
findings.reproduction: Construct KnowledgeBase from core batch definitions and call model_context('HKLM\SOFTWARE\Classes\CLSID\<CLSID>\LocalServer32', ''). The result has value_knowledge=[], while supplying '(Default)' returns one entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Represent an unnamed value with an empty actual name (or an explicit unnamed-value flag), keep a display label separate, and permit value_name='' to match it. Keep None meaning no value supplied. Do not universally rewrite the literal name '(Default)' because a registry value may actually have that name. Add coverage distinguishing unnamed and literal '(Default)' values.

findings.issue: Model exports lose semantic relation explanations and source URLs. The snapshot records these fields, but exported edge-index JSON and edges.csv preserve only endpoints/type/kind/splits, while node-records contain no semantic relation records. External graph consumers cannot recover why a semantic link exists or its evidence from the exported dataset.
findings.reproduction: Render the test graph containing the semantic explanation 'Distinct fixture scopes, not physical-key equivalence.'. This string appears in none of render_model_data(graph()).values(); its semantic edge has only kind/source/target/type.
findings.suggested_fix: Export complete semantic edge records including stable endpoint IDs, relation, explanation and source URLs, for example graph/semantic-edges.jsonl. Keep compact edge indexes as a derived representation and include the full relation records in the manifest.

findings.issue: A modified old manifest can authorize deletion of arbitrary ordinary files inside the dataset directory. The exporter checks hashes for every manifest entry, accepts names outside its generated file set, then unlinks entries absent from the new render. This bypasses the claimed protection of unmanaged/personal files when the manifest was edited or corrupted.
findings.reproduction: Export the test graph into a temporary directory, create personal.txt, add its path and correct SHA-256 to manifest['files'], and export again. The call succeeds and personal.txt is deleted.
findings.suggested_fix: Before any write or deletion, reject old manifest names outside the fixed managed dataset paths (or a strictly validated manifest format/version inventory). Detect unexpected manifest changes rather than treating arbitrary manifest keys as deletion authority. Preserve unmanaged files even if they are listed by an untrusted edited manifest.
